Esigie.fact: Esigie, born Osawe and also rendered as Oseigie, was the sixteenth Oba ('king') of the Kingdom of Benin, ruling during the first half of the sixteenth century until his death around 1550.

Esigie.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Esigie.question: Osawe's claim was opposed by his half-brother _____, who was based at Udo town and supported by groups that resisted Osawe's accession
Esigie.fact: Osawe's claim was opposed by his half-brother Arhuaran, who was based at Udo town and supported by groups that resisted Osawe's accession.

Esigie.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Esigie.question: Benin traditions assign his mother, _____, a military, political and ritual role in securing his victory
Esigie.fact: Benin traditions assign his mother, Idia, a military, political and ritual role in securing his victory.

Esigie.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Esigie.question: He also defeated the hereditary _____ nobles ('kingmakers'), who subsequently submitted to his authority
Esigie.fact: He also defeated the hereditary Uzama nobles ('kingmakers'), who subsequently submitted to his authority.

Esigie.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Esigie.question: Colonial and early scholarly records preserve further variants, including Esige, Asije, Asijie and _____
Esigie.fact: Colonial and early scholarly records preserve further variants, including Esige, Asije, Asijie and Assigie.

Esigie.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Esigie.question: The chronology derived from Egharevba assigns Esigie's reign to approximately _____–1550, a range followed by several later writers
Esigie.fact: The chronology derived from Egharevba assigns Esigie's reign to approximately 1504–1550, a range followed by several later writers.

Esigie.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Esigie.question: Historian Kathryn Wysocki Gunsch uses an accession date of about _____ in her analysis of the palace plaques, while noting that her argument does not depend on establishing an exact year
Esigie.fact: Anthropologist Robert Bradbury regarded the sequence as uncertain and suggested that Esigie may have succeeded Ozolua around 1517, partly because Portuguese evidence places the Oba on campaign in 1516 and may indicate a royal death or transition soon afterwards. Historian Kathryn Wysocki Gunsch uses an accession date of about 1517 in her analysis of the palace plaques, while noting that her argument does not depend on establishing an exact year.

Esigie.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine

Esigie.fact: Anthropologist Robert Bradbury regarded the sequence as uncertain and suggested that Esigie may have succeeded Ozolua around 1517, partly because Portuguese evidence places the Oba on campaign in 1516 and may indicate a royal death or transition soon afterwards. Historian Kathryn Wysocki Gunsch uses an accession date of about 1517 in her analysis of the palace plaques, while noting that her argument does not depend on establishing an exact year.

Esigie.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Esigie.question: Curnow dates the principal Idah campaign to approximately _____–1521, rather than the 1515–1517 range adopted in other reconstructions
Esigie.fact: Curnow dates the principal Idah campaign to approximately 1519–1521, rather than the 1515–1517 range adopted in other reconstructions.

Esigie.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Esigie.question: European documentation provides dates and observations concerning warfare, diplomacy and commerce, but its authors had limited knowledge of _____'s internal politics
Esigie.fact: Historical reconstruction of Esigie's rule depends on Benin oral traditions, palace ceremonies, European missionary and commercial records, royal artworks and archaeological findings. European documentation provides dates and observations concerning warfare, diplomacy and commerce, but its authors had limited knowledge of Benin's internal politics.

Esigie.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Esigie.question: Anthropologist Joseph Eboreime treats _____ as a useful point for comparing oral tradition, documentary records, archaeology and art history in the study of Benin and neighbouring Edo-speaking societi
Esigie.fact: Anthropologist Joseph Eboreime treats 1515 as a useful point for comparing oral tradition, documentary records, archaeology and art history in the study of Benin and neighbouring Edo-speaking societies.

Esigie.fact: Benin traditions identify Arhuaran as his half-brother and principal competitor for the kingship. One group of narratives states that Osawe and Arhuaran were born either on the same day or within a short interval, but that news of Osawe's birth reached the palace record first.

Esigie.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Esigie.question: Another son, _____, appears in the traditions as Ozolua's first designated heir before a physical injury disqualified him from the succession
Esigie.fact: Another son, Ogidogbo, appears in the traditions as Ozolua's first designated heir before a physical injury disqualified him from the succession. In Curnow's account, Arhuaran's mother, Ohomwin, gave birth to her son first but delayed announcing the birth because Ogidogbo was already recognised as heir, whereas Idia immediately informed the palace of Osawe's arrival.

Esigie.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine

Esigie.fact: One group of narratives states that Osawe and Arhuaran were born either on the same day or within a short interval, but that news of Osawe's birth reached the palace record first. In Curnow's account, Arhuaran's mother, Ohomwin, gave birth to her son first but delayed announcing the birth because Ogidogbo was already recognised as heir, whereas Idia immediately informed the palace of Osawe's arrival.

Esigie.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Esigie.question: Academic Josephine Abbe likewise reports that _____ was born first but that Osawe obtained the recognised rights of an heir because his birth was announced earlier
Esigie.fact: One group of narratives states that Osawe and Arhuaran were born either on the same day or within a short interval, but that news of Osawe's birth reached the palace record first. In Curnow's account, Arhuaran's mother, Ohomwin, gave birth to her son first but delayed announcing the birth because Ogidogbo was already recognised as heir, whereas Idia immediately informed the palace of Osawe's arrival.

Esigie.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Esigie.question: Curnow's version presents _____ as the eldest prince and original successor under primogeniture
Esigie.fact: In Curnow's account, Arhuaran's mother, Ohomwin, gave birth to her son first but delayed announcing the birth because Ogidogbo was already recognised as heir, whereas Idia immediately informed the palace of Osawe's arrival. Esigie.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Esigie.question: Ozolua therefore appointed _____ to govern a provincial territory and formally designated Osawe as heir, while chiefs who knew that Arhuaran was older organised a competing faction
Esigie.fact: Curnow's version presents Ogidogbo as the eldest prince and original successor under primogeniture. Ozolua therefore appointed Ogidogbo to govern a provincial territory and formally designated Osawe as heir, while chiefs who knew that Arhuaran was older organised a competing faction.

Esigie.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Esigie.question: The traditions contrast Osawe's intelligence and interest in _____ knowledge with Arhuaran's physical stature, strength and military reputation
Esigie.fact: The traditions contrast Osawe's intelligence and interest in Portuguese knowledge with Arhuaran's physical stature, strength and military reputation. In the same narrative, Osawe's advantages consisted of his education, his ties to a small group of armed Portuguese residents and Idia's ritual expertise.

Esigie.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Esigie.question: In the same narrative, Osawe's advantages consisted of his education, his ties to a small group of armed _____ residents and Idia's ritual expertise
Esigie.fact: The traditions contrast Osawe's intelligence and interest in Portuguese knowledge with Arhuaran's physical stature, strength and military reputation. In the same narrative, Osawe's advantages consisted of his education, his ties to a small group of armed Portuguese residents and Idia's ritual expertise.

Esigie.question: Curnow states that Osawe had already recruited _____ supporters before Ozolua died
Esigie.fact: The traditions contrast Osawe's intelligence and interest in Portuguese knowledge with Arhuaran's physical stature, strength and military reputation. In the same narrative, Osawe's advantages consisted of his education, his ties to a small group of armed Portuguese residents and Idia's ritual expertise.

Esigie.question: Ozolua established _____ at Udo town, a political centre comparable to the Benin capital in size and influence
Esigie.fact: Ozolua set up Arhuaran at Udo town, a political centre comparable to the Benin capital in size and influence. Esigie.question: Curnow records a tradition in which Ozolua provided _____ with an adviser, titled followers, artisans, royal insignia, a large bead symbolising authority and a ritually prepared eben sword
Esigie.fact: Ozolua set up Arhuaran at Udo town, a political centre comparable to the Benin capital in size and influence. Esigie.question: Osawe allegedly persuaded _____ to disclose this instruction and then induced him to lower the sword at a shrine within the Benin capital, preventing Udo from acquiring the intended ritual precedence
Esigie.fact: Ozolua set up Arhuaran at Udo town, a political centre comparable to the Benin capital in size and influence. Curnow records a tradition in which Ozolua provided Arhuaran with an adviser, titled followers, artisans, royal insignia, a large bead symbolising authority and a ritually prepared eben sword.

Esigie.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Esigie.question: He was told not to allow the blade's point to touch the ground before reaching Udo, because the first place where it struck the earth would become the "_____"
Esigie.fact: He was told not to allow the blade's point to touch the ground before reaching Udo, because the first place where it struck the earth would become the "New Benin".

Esigie.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Esigie.question: Osawe's supporters reportedly sent an elaborate false funeral procession through Udo while _____'s remains were concealed inside a plain bundle carried by poorly dressed men
Esigie.fact: Ozolua died while absent from the capital, after which possession and burial of his remains became part of the succession struggle. Osawe's supporters reportedly sent an elaborate false funeral procession through Udo while Ozolua's remains were concealed inside a plain bundle carried by poorly dressed men.

Esigie.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Esigie.question: Arhuaran detained the decorated party, but the body reached _____, who completed his father's funerary rites
Esigie.fact: Osawe's supporters reportedly sent an elaborate false funeral procession through Udo while Ozolua's remains were concealed inside a plain bundle carried by poorly dressed men. Arhuaran detained the decorated party, but the body reached Osawe, who completed his father's funerary rites.

Esigie.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Esigie.question: Egharevba locates an important battle at Okuo-Ukpoba ('battle of blood') and states that _____'s son Oni-oni was killed during the fighting
Esigie.fact: Arhuaran detained the decorated party, but the body reached Osawe, who completed his father's funerary rites. Osawe was then crowned under the regnal name Esigie, and his rivalry with Arhuaran developed into civil war.

Esigie.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Esigie.question: Arhuaran was eventually defeated and drowned in waters remembered as _____ n'Udo
Esigie.fact: Arhuaran was eventually defeated and drowned in waters remembered as Odighi n'Udo.

Esigie.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Esigie.question: Academic Omotade Adegbindin states that she assembled an army when _____ attempted to kill or displace her son and then helped consolidate his possession of the throne
Esigie.fact: Egharevba locates an important battle at Okuo-Ukpoba ('battle of blood') and states that Arhuaran's son Oni-oni was killed during the fighting. Arhuaran was eventually defeated and drowned in waters remembered as Odighi n'Udo.

Esigie.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Esigie.question: Curnow places two early confrontations of the civil war at _____ within Udo territory
Esigie.fact: Curnow places two early confrontations of the civil war at Unuame within Udo territory. Archaeologist Patrick Darling found an unusual quantity of pottery fragments along the Unuame shore and interpreted the deposit as evidence of a large temporary occupation during the early sixteenth century.

Esigie.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Esigie.question: Forced towards a lake, _____ reportedly chose drowning over capture
Esigie.fact: In Curnow's account, Esigie's enlarged army marched against Udo and killed Arhuaran's wife and only son. Forced towards a lake, Arhuaran reportedly chose drowning over capture.

Esigie.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Esigie.question: During the ceremony, the _____ commands destructive forces to depart the Benin capital for Udo, preserving a ritual reference to Arhuaran's continuing hostility after his death
Esigie.fact: During the ceremony, the Esogban commands destructive forces to depart the Benin capital for Udo, preserving a ritual reference to Arhuaran's continuing hostility after his death.

Esigie.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Esigie.question: Egharevba records another conflict involving _____, followed by the destruction of Udo and further operations west of Benin
Esigie.fact: Egharevba records another conflict involving Osemwughe, followed by the destruction of Udo and further operations west of Benin.

Esigie.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Esigie.question: Their settlements lay outside the main defensive earthworks, and each _____ exercised authority over dependent villages and followers
Esigie.fact: Their settlements lay outside the main defensive earthworks, and each Uzama exercised authority over dependent villages and followers. Dynastic accounts describe repeated attempts by early Obas to reduce Uzama control over kingship.

Esigie.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Esigie.question: Their hereditary offices and ritual duties distinguished them from the appointed _____ n'Ore ('town chiefs') and Eghaevbo n'Ogbe ('palace chiefs')
Esigie.fact: Their hereditary offices and ritual duties distinguished them from the appointed Eghaevbo n'Ore ('town chiefs') and Eghaevbo n'Ogbe ('palace chiefs').

Esigie.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Esigie.question: Dynastic accounts describe repeated attempts by early _____ to reduce Uzama control over kingship
Esigie.fact: Dynastic accounts describe repeated attempts by early Obas to reduce Uzama control over kingship.

Esigie.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Esigie.question: The earlier _____ was reportedly responsible for moving the palace away from their settlements and appointing commoners to titled positions as a counterweight to the hereditary nobility
Esigie.fact: The earlier Oba Ewedo was reportedly responsible for moving the palace away from their settlements and appointing commoners to titled positions as a counterweight to the hereditary nobility.

Esigie.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Esigie.question: The original _____ eventually submitted and regained their hereditary positions and ceremonial obligations
Esigie.fact: Esigie responded by appointing a substitute group, which historian Kathryn Wysocki Gunsch identifies as the Uzama n'Ibie. The original Uzama eventually submitted and regained their hereditary positions and ceremonial obligations.

Esigie.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Esigie.question: The Oliha, who headed the _____, received induction directly from the Oba, while the Iyase installed the remaining members
Esigie.fact: The original Uzama eventually submitted and regained their hereditary positions and ceremonial obligations. The Oliha, who headed the Uzama, received induction directly from the Oba, while the Iyase installed the remaining members.

Esigie.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Esigie.question: During the mock combat, the _____ wear their elongated oro headgear, while the Oba displays his coral-beaded crown, or erhu ivie
Esigie.fact: The Oliha, who headed the Uzama, received induction directly from the Oba, while the Iyase installed the remaining members. Traditions concerning the period after Esigie no longer depict the Uzama as a substantial political or military alternative to the throne.

Esigie.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Esigie.question: The Edogun first attempts to persuade the _____ to yield, after which the opposing groups perform four advances and withdrawals using arrows, bows, spears and shields
Esigie.fact: Traditions concerning the period after Esigie no longer depict the Uzama as a substantial political or military alternative to the throne. During the mock combat, the Uzama wear their elongated oro headgear, while the Oba displays his coral-beaded crown, or erhu ivie.

Esigie.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Esigie.question: The Uzama then surrender, offer homage and receive the ruler's blessing, while the _____ signals victory by raising his sword
Esigie.fact: The Edogun first attempts to persuade the Uzama to yield, after which the opposing groups perform four advances and withdrawals using arrows, bows, spears and shields. The Uzama then surrender, offer homage and receive the ruler's blessing, while the Edogun signals victory by raising his sword.

Esigie.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Esigie.question: Several reconstructions place it between approximately _____ and 1517
Esigie.fact: Several reconstructions place it between approximately 1515 and 1517.

Esigie.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Esigie.question: Curnow instead assigns the decisive operations to around _____–1521
Esigie.fact: Curnow instead assigns the decisive operations to around 1519–1521.

Esigie.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Esigie.question: Egharevba explains the invasion through a plot involving the senior chief Oliha, his wife _____ and the Attah of Igala
Esigie.fact: Egharevba explains the invasion through a plot involving the senior chief Oliha, his wife Imaguero and the Attah of Igala. In that account, the Oliha sought external support against Esigie after being deceived in connection with Imaguero's alleged relationship with the ruler.

Esigie.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Esigie.question: Nzegwu interprets the _____ narrative as part of a larger struggle over succession and the political authority of the Uzama
Esigie.fact: Egharevba explains the invasion through a plot involving the senior chief Oliha, his wife Imaguero and the Attah of Igala. In that account, the Oliha sought external support against Esigie after being deceived in connection with Imaguero's alleged relationship with the ruler.

Esigie.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Esigie.question: Curnow similarly associates the invasion with the Oliha and remaining supporters of _____
Esigie.fact: Curnow similarly associates the invasion with the Oliha and remaining supporters of Arhuaran.

Esigie.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Esigie.question: He places it within wider political and commercial rivalry involving _____, the middle Niger, Nupe and Oyo
Esigie.fact: He places it within wider political and commercial rivalry involving Idah, the middle Niger, Nupe and Oyo.

Esigie.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Esigie.question: Ryder also relates the conflict to shifts in Benin's relationship with the sacred authority known as _____ and to competition over regional trade
Esigie.fact: Ryder also relates the conflict to shifts in Benin's relationship with the sacred authority called Oghene and to competition over regional trade.

Esigie.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Esigie.question: Portuguese reports place Europeans in the company of the Oba during military campaigning in _____
Esigie.fact: Portuguese reports place Europeans in the company of the Oba during military campaigning in 1516. Duarte Pires's letter dated 20 October 1516 records missionaries and other Portuguese travelling with the Oba during military operations.

Esigie.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Esigie.question: Duarte Pires's letter dated 20 October _____ records missionaries and other Portuguese travelling with the Oba during military operations
Esigie.fact: Portuguese reports place Europeans in the company of the Oba during military campaigning in 1516. Duarte Pires's letter dated 20 October 1516 records missionaries and other Portuguese travelling with the Oba during military operations.

Esigie.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Esigie.question: Some traditions describe _____ cannon or other firearms as decisive in the victory
Esigie.fact: Portuguese reports place Europeans in the company of the Oba during military campaigning in 1516. One account stated that a shipmaster had seen a European resident accompanying the ruler to war early that year, while a second report from October again located Portuguese men with him during a campaign against Igala.

Esigie.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Esigie.question: Historian Ray Kea considers it possible that _____ arquebusiers accompanied the army but argues that Benin's soldiers did not possess firearms during the campaign
Esigie.fact: Some traditions describe Portuguese cannon or other firearms as decisive in the victory. Academics Peter Roese and Ronald Smith record a version in which the Igala began retreating after a Portuguese gunner, or possibly a German serving with the Portuguese, fired a cannon near the Oregbeni Hills.

Esigie.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Esigie.question: Curnow considers both the baptism account and its connection with _____-Osa potentially apocryphal or conjectural
Esigie.fact: One tradition concerning Ague places the ritual within Esigie's military camp, where it was used to strengthen his forces. In this account, the defeated Attah and his army were required to kneel and repent before Portuguese companions of Esigie baptised them at the conclusion of Ague-Osa.

Esigie.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Esigie.question: Some captured Igala soldiers were castrated and incorporated into the _____ guild, serving either in the Oba's harem or at the Iyoba's palace in Uselu
Esigie.fact: Some captured Igala soldiers were castrated and incorporated into the Eguadase guild, serving either in the Oba's harem or at the Iyoba's palace in Uselu. An Ekasa verse recorded by Bradbury states that both Eguadase and Ogbelaka supplied Ewua officials and that Eguadase maintained an altar dedicated to Esigie.

Esigie.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Esigie.question: Leopard symbolism represented both the _____ and the Attah of Igala
Esigie.fact: Leopard symbolism represented both the Benin Oba and the Attah of Igala.

Esigie.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Esigie.question: A _____ joke about the Igala defeat altered the Attah's title to Attah n'akpa ('Attah the fool') through wordplay involving atalakpa
Esigie.fact: Leopard symbolism represented both the Benin Oba and the Attah of Igala. A Benin joke about the Igala defeat altered the Attah's title to Attah n'akpa ('Attah the fool') through wordplay involving atalakpa.

Esigie.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Esigie.question: Brass bird-shaped idiophones and palace representations subsequently became associated with the victory and the _____ festival
Esigie.fact: Brass bird-shaped idiophones and palace representations subsequently became associated with the victory and the Ugie Oro festival. Curnow argues that Esigie inserted the bird episode into an older Ugie Oro observance rather than originating the festival itself.

Esigie.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Esigie.question: Ryder argues that the victory altered _____'s relationship with Idah and reinforced the Oba's influence in the Niger region
Esigie.fact: Ryder argues that the victory altered Benin's relationship with Idah and reinforced the Oba's influence in the Niger region.

Esigie.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Esigie.question: Egharevba connects the phrase Emwa n'Udo with the name "Ondo" and suggests that _____'s title may have developed into "Osemawe", the title borne by rulers of the Ondo Kingdom
Esigie.fact: Egharevba connects the phrase Emwa n'Udo with the name "Ondo" and suggests that Osemwughe's title may have developed into "Osemawe", the title borne by rulers of the Ondo Kingdom.

Esigie.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Esigie.question: Academic Eben Sheba records a tradition in which the two princes were born on the same day, _____'s birth was announced first and Abodi Jabado was thereafter authorised to found a separate kingdom
Esigie.fact: Academic Eben Sheba records a tradition in which the two princes were born on the same day, Orhogbua's birth was announced first and Abodi Jabado was thereafter authorised to found a separate kingdom.

Esigie.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Esigie.question: The royal insignia assigned to the _____ included a crown, the ọ̀pá-ìdìkòbà, an adá sword and an abẹ̀nrẹ̀n

Another states that the Abodi was Esigie's concealed first-born child by a non-Edo wife and was removed after a different prince received recognition as heir.

Esigie.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Esigie.question: Traditions variously associate the migration route with Arogbo-Ile, _____, Ode-Irele and other Ikale communities
Esigie.fact: Traditions variously associate the migration route with Arogbo-Ile, Akotogbo, Ode-Irele and other Ikale communities.

Esigie.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Esigie.question: Academic Oluwakemi Adesina associates the name "_____" with the military camp "Eko-Aile", while treating the derivation as part of regional tradition
Esigie.fact: Traditions variously associate the migration route with Arogbo-Ile, Akotogbo, Ode-Irele and other Ikale communities. Academic Oluwakemi Adesina associates the name "Ikale" with the military camp "Eko-Aile", while treating the derivation as part of regional tradition.

Esigie.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Esigie.question: Ikale histories also preserve accounts of earlier movement from Ife and of several migrations rather than descent from a single _____ foundation
Esigie.fact: Ikale histories also preserve accounts of earlier movement from Ife and of several migrations rather than descent from a single Benin foundation.

Esigie.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Esigie.question: Osadolor identifies an Iyase called Odia as a battlefield commander in _____ and associates another officer, Emovon, with reconquest and territorial consolidation
Esigie.fact: Osadolor identifies an Iyase called Odia as a battlefield commander in 1515 and associates another officer, Emovon, with reconquest and territorial consolidation.

Esigie.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Esigie.question: The war drum known as Em'Ighan was attributed to Atakparhakpa in early _____ and used to transmit commands during campaigns
Esigie.fact: The war drum called Em'Ighan was attributed to Atakparhakpa in early 1516 and used to transmit commands during campaigns.

Esigie.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Esigie.question: Enslaved people served in _____ as troops, household retainers and members of specialised royal establishments
Esigie.fact: Enslaved people served in Benin as troops, household retainers and members of specialised royal establishments.

Esigie.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Esigie.question: Some attained positions of command, including the officer associated with _____'s contingent
Esigie.fact: Some attained positions of command, including the officer associated with Idia's contingent.

Esigie.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Esigie.question: Historian Osarhieme Osadolor dates such a restriction to about _____ and states that convicted persons, war captives and women remained available for sale
Esigie.fact: Historian Osarhieme Osadolor dates such a restriction to about 1516 and states that convicted persons, war captives and women remained available for sale.

Esigie.question: Portuguese records document repeated attempts by _____ to acquire firearms
Esigie.fact: Egharevba states that firearms were first employed in Benin while he ruled. Portuguese records document repeated attempts by Benin to acquire firearms.

Esigie.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Esigie.question: In _____ or 1514, the reigning Oba ordered the seizure of a cannon from a Portuguese caravel
Esigie.fact: In 1513 or 1514, the reigning Oba ordered the seizure of a cannon from a Portuguese caravel.

Esigie.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Esigie.question: Kea identifies that monarch as Esigie, whereas chronologies dating his accession to about _____ would place the event under Ozolua
Esigie.fact: Kea identifies that monarch as Esigie, whereas chronologies dating his accession to about 1517 would place the event under Ozolua.

Esigie.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Esigie.question: Ryder suggested that the ruler may have intended _____ metalworkers to examine the weapon, although reproducing a comparable cannon locally would have presented substantial technical difficulties

Gaskiya Ta Fi Kwabo.fact: Since there was no major newspaper in the North as compared to the South, the Government therefore concluded on setting up a vernacular newspaper which was to be called Gaskiya Tafi Kwabo.

Gastrointestinal physiology.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Gastrointestinal physiology.question: The _____ was Study of the physical function of the gut.
Gastrointestinal physiology.fact: Gastrointestinal physiology is the branch of human physiology that addresses the physical function of the gastrointestinal (GI) tract.

Gastrointestinal physiology.subject: Ayurveda & Traditional Medicine
Gastrointestinal physiology.question: Most of the HCO3− comes from pancreatic acinar cells in the form of _____3 in an aqueous solution
Gastrointestinal physiology.fact: Most of the HCO3− comes from pancreatic acinar cells in the form of NaHCO3 in an aqueous solution.
